Why AUROVA

Fewer shirts.
Worn more.

Most shirts are designed to be bought, not worn. AUROVA works the other way — every piece is built around the parts that actually wear out first: the collar stand, the yoke, the top three buttons. Fix those, and a shirt outlasts the season it was cut for.

We keep runs small on purpose. A pattern gets adjusted after every batch, based on what the last one got wrong. That's slower than most labels are willing to go. It's also the only way we know to get a shirt that fits like it was actually made for you.

From Cloth to Collar

How a shirt
actually gets made.

No mystery here — just the four stages every AUROVA shirt goes through before it reaches the rail, in the order they actually happen.

01 — Source
Cloth, chosen first

We pick the fabric roll before we sketch a single seam — the cloth decides what the shirt is allowed to become.

02 — Cut
Pattern, then blade

Each panel is cut against the grain by hand, so the collar and cuffs hang the same way years later.

03 — Stitch
Single tailor, one shirt

One tailor sees a shirt from first stitch to last button, not a line of hands each doing one seam.

04 — Inspect
Worn before it's sold

Every shirt is worn for a full day on the floor before it's tagged and shelved. If it chafes, it doesn't ship.
